name: Iron-deficiency anaemia
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> Iron-deficiency anaemia / low haemoglobin or low iron. Check question: Has a doctor or lab report told you that you have anaemia or low iron (low haemoglobin or low ferritin)? Yes, iron-deficiency anaemia / Yes, low ferritin but normal haemoglobin / Yes, anaemia but cause not known / Borderline (lifestyle-only mode) / No / Never tested (suggest a blood test) / Not sure. Follow-ups: pregnant or planning pregnancy; heavy or long periods; black or bloody stools; on iron tablets or IFA (name and doctor-set dose, stored only); diet (vegetarian, vegan, Jain, egg, non-veg); tea or coffee with meals; optional latest haemoglobin, ferritin, MCV, test date.

conflictsWith.rule: Pregnancy: IFA dose and anaemia treatment are doctor-led; app sets no iron dose; requires_doctor_input
Chronic kidney disease: anaemia treatment (oral or IV iron, ESA) set by kidney doctor; P13 limits override
Jain diet: no meat, no root vegetables; use dals, bajra, ragi, leafy greens, seeds, vitamin C; iron plus B12 check
Vegan diet: non-heme iron only; NIH suggests about 1.8 times the usual intake (secondary); B12 check; doctor-led supplements
Celiac disease is a common cause of unexplained iron deficiency; doctor tests; gluten-free filter must not remove iron foods
Calcium plans: keep calcium supplements and iron tablets apart (ask doctor or pharmacist)
Fat loss: no deficit that drops iron-rich foods; heavy-period users should not crash-diet

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose anaemia or iron deficiency.
The app never sets an iron tablet, IFA or injection dose; treatment doses are doctor-set and can exceed the 45 mg/day upper limit.
Do not start iron tablets on tiredness alone: confirm with a blood test, because B12 or folate deficiency, thalassaemia trait and chronic disease also cause anaemia.
Iron overdose is an emergency in children; keep tablets out of reach and call a doctor or poison centre at once.
Pallor with breathlessness at rest, chest pain, fainting, black or bloody stools, heavy bleeding, pregnancy, or a child with anaemia: see a doctor promptly.
Men and postmenopausal women with iron deficiency need a doctor to look for hidden blood loss.
Thalassaemia trait or haemochromatosis: do not take iron without medical advice.
